claims.text: Applying a machine-learning-optimized refractory HEA coating by laser cladding will significantly improve the corrosion resistance of stainless steel in extreme corrosive environments.
Unmodified stainless steel has reduced corrosion resistance under extreme conditions.
Machine-learning analysis of HEA composition, deposition, and post-treatment data can identify an optimal coating formulation and processing protocol.
A refractory HEA coating can be deposited onto a steel substrate by laser cladding.
The proposed coating will improve performance during high-temperature molten-salt exposure or other aggressive chemical conditions.
The optimized coating will have a nanocrystalline, refined microstructure.
Increasing Cr content in a refractory HEA coating promotes grain refinement and changes its phase constitution.
The Cr-associated phases in the optimized coating are protective against corrosion.
The refined coating microstructure minimizes micro-galvanic coupling and surface defect sites.
The nanocrystalline, phase-tuned coating enhances chemical stability.
The optimized coating has enhanced adhesion to stainless steel.
Enhanced chemical stability and adhesion mitigate localized corrosion mechanisms.
The optimized coating will produce a lower corrosion rate than unmodified or conventionally coated stainless steel.
The optimized coating will produce a more positive corrosion potential than the baselines.
The optimized coating will retain stable microstructural features during corrosive exposure.
Long-term adhesion and performance under cyclic thermal or mechanical stresses have not been established.
The quantitative corrosion improvement is uncertain and may depend on environmental conditions and exposure duration.
